chip.description: Motorola 68000 with on-die opcode decryption; the 8 KB key lives in battery-backed internal RAM, so the part stops running the game when the battery dies (taxonomy §6 adjudication: an encrypted 68000 is a 68000).
chip.notes: src/mame/sega/fd1094.cpp in MAME 0.288 ("The FD1094 is a custom CPU based on the 68000, which runs encrypted code. The decryption key is stored in 8KB of battery-backed RAM"). Manufacturer follows MAME's device full name, "Hitachi FD1094 Encrypted CPU"; the module was supplied to Sega, which catalogues it under its own 317-xxxx key numbers.
